his is my last thesis of the day.
While the rest of the timeline is still debating whether PHP2Shell is “just another patch” or the closest thing the web has seen to a mass RCE since Log4j, $PHP (PHP-UP-2026) already turned the story into a chart.
PHP powers a huge percentage of the internet (WordPress, Drupal, Magento, custom stacks, everything). Two critical unauthenticated RCEs (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619) in session.upload_progress just got emergency-patched on Oct 21. Pre-auth, default config, worker memory corruption / UAF paths that can lead to code execution or memory disclosure. Researchers were circulating PoCs, sites were taking themselves offline as a precaution, and the “steal everything, leave nothing” meme energy was immediate. The token’s branding (skull + “Steal Everything / Leave Nothing”) is locked to that exact moment.

•  ATH already over $2M

•  Mint and freeze revoked, classic graduated pump.fun profile
This isn’t a quiet micro-cap. It’s a narrative token riding a real, high-visibility security event that is still being written about in security blogs, GitHub repos, and news headlines right now. When the broader market sees “PHP” + exploit + RCE + mass websites at risk, the search volume and the meme volume both hit at the same time. That’s the setup.
I’m the top holder. I watched the holder count cross 5k while the story was still fresh. The chart has already shown it can move hard on the narrative. If this keeps the attention of the security/meme crossover crowd and the volume stays elevated, the next legs come from people realizing this is the cleanest ticker attached to the actual event, not a random copy.
